                "description": "...The National Weather Service in Norman has issued a Flood Warning\nfor the following rivers in Texas...Oklahoma...\n\nRed River near Burkburnett affecting Clay, Wichita, Tillman,\nJefferson and Cotton Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Red River near Burkburnett.\n\n* WHEN...From Sunday morning to Sunday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Crop and range lands... oil fields... and\nrural roads are affected. Some low-lying areas near the river may\nbe isolated by high water in side channels. Bottomlands near\nDavidson Oklahoma begin to flood several hours before the crest\napproaches the Burkburnett area. The flood crest reaches the area\nalong the river near Taylor Oklahoma several hours later. Cattle\nand other property should be relocated to places which are higher\nthan nearby river banks to avoid being stranded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:30 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 7.4 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 9.0 feet\ntomorrow morning. Rip currents can sweep even the best\nswimmers away from shore into deeper water.",
                "instruction": "High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing\nlocalized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.\nSwimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking\nwaves and dangerous surf conditions.\n\nRip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away\nfrom shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the\nsandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and\npiers.                 "headline": "Flood Warning issued October 17 at 9:04AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL",
                "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...\n\nSt Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.\n\n.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to remain in Minor Flood\nStage today, then strong northeasterly winds will slow river flow\nleading to a quick rise in levels. The river is forecast to reach\nModerate Flood Stage late Sunday to early Monday, with a steady\nincrease through Moderate Flood Stage forecast next week.\n\nFor the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 2.3 feet, Many docks become submerged along the river\nand in canals in the Astor community. Water enters yards of\nproperties on Bartram Road, Holiday Circle and along Wild Hog Road\non the Lake County side. In Volusia County, water encroaches yards\nof homes on the river side of Alice Drive. No wake zones are in\neffect from near the South Moon Canal to approximately 800 feet\nsouth of the Riverview lodge. At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps\ncovered at South Moon Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's\nJungle Den. Water approaching sites closest to the river at Fish\nTales RV Resort and Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair\nStreet covered by river water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks\nunderwater at the Astor Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive.\nPortions of Fox Road are covered with water nearest to the river.\nAcorn, Hazelnut and Redbud roads are underwater with yards\ninundated. At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes\non or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the\nparking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of\nAlligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue\nCreek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake\nDexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest\nto the river on McPherson Lane. At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed\ninto yards. Homes on or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become\ninaccessible with several inches of water inside homes along the\nriver and canals. Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor\nare completely submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are\ninaccessible with yards completely submerged. Clair Street is\ninaccessible. Roads flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and\nyards at condominiums on Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall\nat Blair's Jungle Den.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:30 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 2.5 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 8:30 AM EDT Saturday was 2.6 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.3 feet early next\nweek following a period of persistent northeasterly winds.\nAdditional rises are possible thereafter.\n- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

                "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued October 17 at 3:27AM CDT until October 17 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA",
                "description": "...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS POSSIBLE TODAY...\n\n.A cold front is introducing some very dry air with RH values\nfalling into the low to mid 30s along with windy conditions with\nsome gusts well into the 30 mph range. The dry, breezy conditions will remain\ncausing favorable conditions for fire spread.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Pointe Coupee, West Feliciana, East Feliciana,\nSt. Helena, Washington, Iberville, West Baton Rouge, East\nBaton Rouge, Assumption, St. James, Wilkinson, Amite, Pike,\nNorthern Tangipahoa, Walthall, Southeast St. Tammany, Pearl\nRiver, Northern St. Tammany, Southwestern St. Tammany,\nHancock, Central Tangipahoa, Harrison, Lower Tangipahoa,\nJackson, Northern Livingston, Southern Livingston, Western\nAscension and Eastern Ascension.\n\n* WINDS...North 15 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 30 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread\nquickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.",
